stories.summary: A cyber-attack caused refrigeration temperatures to soar to 50C overnight on Monday across several hundred French supermarkets, with widespread food losses reported. At Intermarché La Haye, the attack caused fridge temperatures to reach 27C (80F), spoiling fresh and frozen food, according to store director Julien Freret. stories.title: Hurricane Simon and Tropical Storm Rachel kill five people on Mexico’s Pacific coast
stories.summary: Security forces use helicopters to rescue dozens of people as the two storms damage infrastructure and cause flash flooding At least five people have died after Hurricane Simon and Tropical Storm Rachel pummelled Mexico’s Pacific coast, causing flooding that downed trees and electricity poles, blocked roads and inundated homes. stories.title: Opposition figures and journalists allege police abuses during India protests
stories.summary: The protests were triggered by allegations of manipulating voter lists during a nationwide roll revision that critics say could benefit Prime Minister Narendra Modi's ruling Bharatiya Janata Party.

stories.summary: The White House calls the adverts, reportedly paid for with $20 million of Homeland Security funds, public service announcements, but they have drawn criticism from both parties.

stories.title: Citroën revives its classic 2CV with a new electric concept
stories.summary: Citroën has unveiled an all-electric concept inspired by its iconic 2CV, aiming to bring the classic model back to the road within the next two years. The compact vehicle combines retro styling with modern electric technology and is expected to start at around €15,000.

stories.title: Video shows major fire ravaging 400-year-old Paris food market

stories.title: Paris’s oldest covered food market gutted by major overnight fire
stories.summary: Fire tore through Paris’s oldest covered food market in the Marais, leaving traders devastated. An investigation is under way and the market may stay shut for months.

stories.title: Rent surges in Georgia and Armenia as Russians flee fearing mobilisation
stories.summary: Monthly rents in Yerevan now run to €800–900 for a two-room flat, up 23.5% year on year in August, while Tbilisi rents have stabilised after 60–70% jumps following the full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022. Russian nationals account for 72% of all foreign property transactions in Armenia.

stories.title: US theme park operator Six Flags shuts nine roller coasters after man dies
stories.summary: Police are investigating after TV footage showed riders being evacuated from the 60-metre high Goliath ride.

stories.title: German nationals among those airlifted to safety as storms kill five in Mexico
stories.summary: Heavy rain and strong winds have caused serious damage in Baja California and Guerrero, where authorities seek six missing and deploy thousands of rescue workers amid further flood risk.

stories.title: Ceuta awaits King Felipe after summer migration crisis
stories.summary: Ceuta braces for a symbolic royal visit by King Felipe VI and Queen Letizia after a mass migration crisis strained the enclave’s social cohesion.

stories.title: Zaporizhzhia airstrikes kill 17 as Russia intensifies attacks across Ukraine
stories.summary: Zaporizhzhia was hit by deadly Russian airstrikes on Saturday, 10 October, killing at least 17 people, including three children, Ukrainian officials said. Rescuers searched rubble for survivors as the city faced renewed strikes on residential areas.

stories.title: Houthis claim further Riyadh airport attacks as Saturday’s death toll rises to 13
stories.summary: The Houthis claimed responsibility for the weekend attacks on Riyadh airport. Saturday’s death toll rose to 13, while a further strike on Sunday killed one person. Flights remain suspended as Trump weighs US involvement.

stories.title: Volkswagen boss backs EU plan to bolster domestic European industry
stories.summary: Oliver Blume says ‘Made in Europe’ rules to counter rapid rise of lower-price Chinese brands ‘must reward real value creation’ The boss of Volkswagen has backed EU proposals to boost its domestic industry, arguing European carmakers need to be able to “compete under comparable conditions” with Chinese rivals. Oliver Blume said “Made in Europe” rules from the EU “must reward real value creation in Europe”, speaking in Paris before the motor show this week. Continue reading...

stories.title: Denmark tests humanoid robots in supermarkets to help to ease staff workload at night
stories.summary: Denmark’s Salling Group is trialling Hive Robots in stores to handle demanding restocking, freeing staff for customer service while robots work mainly at night.

stories.title: At least 139 migrants dead after boat capsizes off Djibouti, UN says
stories.summary: The UN's IOM agency says tens of thousands of migrants travel from the Horn of Africa through Djibouti each year as they look to cross the Bab el-Mandeb Strait to Yemen and eventually reach the Gulf countries.

stories.title: Nepal orders evacuations after landslide triggers Budhi Gandaki flash flood
stories.summary: Nepal’s authorities ordered residents along the Budhi Gandaki River to evacuate on Sunday, 11 October, after a sudden flash flood swept away homes and other buildings in the country’s mountainous north-central region.

stories.title: North Korea fires 'several ballistic missiles' into Sea of Japan, Seoul's military says
stories.summary: South Korea's National Security Office convened an emergency security meeting following the launch to review the country's military readiness.

stories.title: Europe Today: Trump claims Ukraine-Russia energy ceasefire as Baltics stay on alert
stories.summary: Donald Trump says Russia and Ukraine have agreed an energy ceasefire. Volodymyr Zelenskyy says it was news to him. As he addresses the Warsaw Security Forum, we hear from Latvia's FM Baiba Braže, Doha after a deadly Riyadh airport attack, and France's debt fears.

stories.title: Egyptian journalists plan weekend protest over detention of six colleagues

stories.title: ICJ judge Navi Pillay wins Nobel peace prize for promoting international law
stories.summary: Committee recognises work of South African who chaired UN commission that concluded Israel was guilty of genocide in Gaza The Nobel peace prize has been awarded to Navi Pillay, the South African former UN human rights chief who chaired the UN commission that concluded Israel was guilty of genocide in Gaza . stories.summary: Recommended dose of hepatitis B vaccine will be withheld from thousands of newborns by Danish researchers A controversial research trial that will withhold hepatitis B vaccines from some African newborns was given approval to move forward this week. stories.summary: Turki Al-Maliki, a spokesperson for the Saudi-led coalition forces, said that the attack had been carried out by Yemen's Houthi rebels and that it had targeted a passenger terminal.

stories.title: Scientists discover 180,000 giant tortoises on one Seychelles island

A population of Aldabra giant tortoises lives on an island in Seychelles called Aldabra Atoll. Continue reading...

stories.title: Isaias strengthens to become first Atlantic hurricane of 2026 season
stories.summary: Storm expected to make landfall on US’s northern Gulf coast with risk of flash floods and isolated river flooding Isaias has become the first Atlantic hurricane of the 2026 season, with wind speeds of 80mph and a minimum pressure of 975mb. It is expected to strengthen to a category 2 hurricane as it approaches the US’s northern Gulf coast on Friday, according to the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA). stories.summary: Isaias made landfall as a Category 2 hurricane in the city of Destin in the Florida Panhandle on Friday evening. It has since weakened into a post-tropical cyclone.

stories.title: Michael Jordan's 1998 NBA Finals sneakers sell for a record $2.2 million
stories.summary: In 1998, Michael Jordan laced up a pair of his iconic black and red Air Jordan 13s to bring home a Bulls victory during Game 2 of his final NBA championship — and now they are the most expensive sneakers ever to sell at auction. The game-winning sneakers sold for $2.2 million at Sotheby's in New York on Tuesday, smashing the sneaker auction record of $1.47 million, set in 2021 by a pair of Nike Air Ships that Jordan wore earlier in his career.

To a crowd of, reportedly, over 125,000 people, Jennie, Jisoo, Lisa and Rosé used the ground-breaking moment to pay homage to Korean heritage by arriving onstage in hanboks: a traditional type of dress.
